messages:
sam_sales: Hey team — acme POC hit a hard blocker. Their app in a private VPC can't reach the Redwood private endpoint. They see timeouts and TLS failures. Can we swarm?

acme_poc_admin: Repro steps: from app pod `curl https://api.redwood.internal:443/v1/health` hangs then TLS error. `dig api.redwood.internal +short` -> `10.2.45.12`. We also have an F5 doing corporate SSL inspection.

maria_se: quick checks: can you `dig +short api.redwood.internal` and try `curl -v --resolve 'api.redwood.cloud:443:10.2.45.12' https://api.redwood.cloud/v1/health`? want to see if SNI fixes it.

acme_poc_admin: dig gave `10.2.45.12`. Ran the --resolve test; with `--resolve` I get `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`. Without --resolve it times out or TLS mismatches.

ryan_sre: that pattern = DNS resolves to private IP but the cert is for our public hostname, so SNI needs to be the public name. Try openssl to inspect cert: `openssl s_client -connect 10.2.45.12:443 -servername api.redwood.cloud` and `openssl s_client -connect 10.2.45.12:443 -servername api.redwood.internal` — see which cert is returned.

acme_poc_admin: pasted openssl output: the cert CN is `*.redwood-cloud.com` and SANs show `DNS:*.redwood-cloud.com`. When we set `-servername api.redwood.cloud` we get the proper cert, but when the app uses internal hostname it fails verify. Also our F5 sometimes replaces certs (shows corporate CA) which I think breaks chain/trust.

alex_support: two likely causes: 1) app is using internal hostname in TLS handshake so SNI doesn't match cert, 2) SSL inspection/proxy replacing cert. Workarounds: a) map app to use the public hostname (api.redwood.cloud) so SNI matches, b) configure F5 for SSL passthrough or bypass for api.redwood.cloud, or c) install company CA into app truststore (if inspection cannot be bypassed).

ingrid_networking: firewall note: their cluster blocks outbound to the internet except approved IP ranges. If they resolved to internal IP (10.2.45.12) that's probably our PrivateLink/NLB in their VPC — confirm whether they have an egress NAT/proxy rewriting SNI. If they plan to talk to public endpoints instead, they need to allow outbound TCP/443 to our public IP ranges.

acme_poc_admin: networking says they cannot disable TLS inspection for a domain, but they *can* whitelist IPs. Can you provide an IP list to whitelist?

maria_se: we'll send the public IP CIDR list privately via the support ticket (don't paste here). Note: if you're using our PrivateLink we can instead provide the endpoint config so traffic stays internal and avoids inspection/egress rules.

ryan_sre: additional troubleshooting commands for the team:
```
# check name resolution from a pod
kubectl exec -it <pod> -- dig +short api.redwood.internal
# check SNI / cert
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.cloud:443 -servername api.redwood.cloud
# simulate app behavior
curl -v --resolve 'api.redwood.cloud:443:10.2.45.12' https://api.redwood.cloud/v1/health
```

alex_support: FYI if the F5 performs SSL interception the cert you see will be the corporate one; in that case you either add the corp CA to the app JVM/truststore or bypass for single FQDN. That is the most common enterprise blocker.

acme_poc_admin: understood — we can add the corp CA to our JVM truststore as a short-term mitigation. Networking says they'll whitelist the IPs if you provide them.

deploybot: Support ticket created: SUP-3289. Assigned to eng-infra. Please move sensitive IP list to the ticket thread.

sam_sales: TL;DR action items: 1) acme will add corp CA to truststore (short term) + confirm, 2) acme networking will whitelist IPs we provide (48h ETA), 3) we will open PrivateLink option if they prefer to avoid egress/inspection, 4) eng will validate once whitelist/CA changes are applied. Scheduling a 30m check-in tomorrow 10:00am PT.

ryan_sre: once whitelist is in place test without `--resolve` and run `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.cloud:443 -servername api.redwood.cloud` to confirm the cert chain and SANs show `*.redwood-cloud.com`. If inspection still present, we'll need F5 passthrough or app CA update.

acme_poc_admin: will run tests and update SUP-3289. Thanks everyone — this unblocks the POC path forward.

sam_sales: great — marking as swarm in progress. :thumbsup:
